source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Regular NSAID use warrants clinician review because NSAIDs can reduce renal blood flow and worsen renal injury, especially when kidney function is impaired.","B":"Daily ibuprofen is preferred in CKD because NSAIDs increase renal blood flow and protect remaining kidney function during long-term use.","C":"Over-the-counter ibuprofen has minimal renal risk in CKD because nonprescription status indicates that daily long-term use is kidney-safe.","D":"Higher ibuprofen doses are safer in CKD because stronger anti-inflammatory effects reduce the likelihood of NSAID-related renal injury."}}
source_row.rationale: FDA ibuprofen labeling warns that long-term NSAID use can cause renal injury and that prostaglandin inhibition can reduce renal blood flow, with greater risk in patients who already have impaired renal function. Option A therefore appropriately prompts review rather than assuming daily OTC use is safe. Options B and D reverse the renal-risk relationship. Option C incorrectly equates nonprescription availability with renal safety.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed Ibuprofen Tablets — Warnings, Renal Effects/Advanced Renal Disease: long-term NSAID administration can cause renal injury; renal prostaglandin inhibition can reduce renal blood flow, with greatest risk in patients with impaired renal function; advanced renal disease requires avoidance or close renal monitoring when treatment is necessary. Current FDA ibuprofen tablet labeling at cited DailyMed set ID; Renal Effects/Advanced Renal Disease sections live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication routes, administration, reversal, adverse effects/interactions, withdrawal, monitoring and client teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client with chronic kidney disease reports taking over-the-counter ibuprofen every day for musculoskeletal pain. Which teaching is most appropriate?
